title: Weather Reports Frozen in Ice
question: How can scientists know Earth's climate from before thermometers existed?
hook: Climate records only go back about 150 years, yet ice cores reach back more than 800,000 years.
idea: Ice, sediments, fossils and other natural records keep traces of past climates that, once dated, let scientists rebuild them.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in order, from snowfall to a measurement of ancient air.
items: Later snow piles on top and its weight presses down
The snow becomes ice, sealing air in tiny bubbles
Scientists measure the trapped air's makeup
beats.explain: Snow is compressed into ice under the weight of later snow, locking air into bubbles that can later be measured directly.

beats.prompt: Match each clue in an ice core to what it reveals.
pairs: What the air was made of
beats.explain: Each part of the core preserves a different record of conditions at the time that layer formed.

beats.prompt: Water with heavy oxygen-18 evaporates at a higher temperature than ordinary water. One ice layer has more oxygen-18 relative to oxygen-16 than another. Other factors aside, what does that suggest?

choices.label: It formed in a colder period
choices.feedback: Tempting if you think heavy water needs cold, but heavy water evaporates more readily when it is warmer.

choices.label: It formed in a warmer period
It formed after a large volcanic eruption
choices.feedback: The oxygen ratio tracks temperature, not eruptions.

choices.label: Nothing, since the ratio never changes
choices.feedback: Cycles in these isotope ratios have been detected, so the ratio does vary.

beats.explain: The oxygen-18 to oxygen-16 ratio rises with temperature, though salinity and ice volume also play a part.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which one?
steps: Comparing recent and older climate records shows how an area's weather has changed.
Such records only began in the mid-1800s.
That leaves researchers about 150 years of data.
So these records alone can map an area's climate 10,000 years ago.
beats.explain: About 150 years of measurements cannot reach back 10,000 years, which is why more complex methods are needed.
